abstract: An important facet of gender detection in surveillance systems is improving security, crowd monitoring, and behavioral analysis. This work explains advanced techniques for gender detection applications using the latest version of the You Only Look Once object detection algorithm called YOLOv8. YOLOv8, known for its real-time processing capacity and increased accuracy, is an efficient tool for surveillance applications. This article discusses YOLOv8 implementation in gender identification in challenging environments. Challenges from lighting conditions, occlusions, and angles of the cameras continue being exposed. Experiments show that YOLOv8 is robust enough to detect and classify gender accordingly using real-time surveillance footage. We also utilized the back body pose for analysis, whereas others employed front face or body poses. The work here provides insights for optimizing model parameters and enhances detection precision. This offers a very valuable tool for modern surveillance systems.

articleTitle: Applying Vision Transformers for Herbal Medicine Classification: A Novel Approach to Plant Identification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: The medicinal plants are particularly important in traditional health care systems, yet the right identification of medicinal plants is one of the great challenges because of diversity and similarity among species. In this paper, we introduce a new approach to herbal medicine classification using Vision Transformers, or simply ViTs. This deep learning architecture is at the front edge of approaching complex patterns within plant images through leveraging self-attention mechanisms. Unlike the classical CNN, Vision Transformers are significantly better than their counterparts on tasks related to classification as they concentrate on global relationships between image patches. We apply and test our model on a comprehensive dataset of medicinal plants. It is demonstrated that Vision Transformer works better in accuracy and generalization than existing CNN-based approaches. In addition, the model demonstrates robustness under different environmental conditions related to lighting, variations of backgrounds, and also other probable challenges in identification with the real world. This study also brings out the possibility of directly integrating the classification system based on Vision Transformers into applications that may be used in mobile devices, which will now enable real-time identification in fieldwork settings for herbal medicines. Our findings show that the proposed Vision Transformers push medicinal plant classification in new directions in traditional and modern medical settings.

articleTitle: Impulsive cardiac death Prediction Model Using Machine Learning and Deep learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: Person suffering from cardiovascular diseases are reasons for unexpected Impulsive cardiac death (ISD). Impulsive cardiac death risk identification can be obtained from Electrocardiogram (ECG).This paper presents machine learning and deep learning approach based intelligent human heart monitoring. Machine learning approach based Heart Rate Variability (HRV) and Wavelet Transform (WT) methods classify obtained data into normal or abnormal subjects. The proposed research can effectively identify risk factors for Impulsive cardiac death. For implementing intelligent learning based cardiovascular diseases risk monitoring system, the proposed method use Naïve Bayes (NB), Decision Tree(DT) and k nearest neighbor (KNN) machine learning classifiers for classification. For this innovative strategy, three classifiers risk identification obtained with highest accuracy of 98.9% (KNN), 98.5(NB) and 99.3 %( DT).The obtained results shows that combined approach HRV and WT are robust and efficient for impulsive cardiac risk identification. CNN-LSTM based deep learning model predicting heart diseases highly accurate when compared to machine learning techniques. Hardware module experiment implemented for testing cardiovascular diseases based on real time ECG signal obtained from patient.

articleTitle: A Novel Methodology to Predict Dental Cavities based on Intensive Deep Learning Strategy
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: Quantitative Light-Induced Fluorescence (Qua-LF) is an objective method for detecting and measuring dental cavity based on plaque using the natural fluorescence properties of bacterial porphyrins. Additionally, complementary artificial intelligence modeling, such as XGBoost, has demonstrated superior predictive accuracy compared to traditional regression models in assessing oral health data. However, the effectiveness of these models heavily relies on the quality and quantity of training data, with larger and more diverse datasets improving accuracy and robustness. Supervised learning, the primary learning technique used in these studies, requires manually annotated datasets, which is time-consuming and labor-intensive. Inconsistencies in image quality, lighting conditions, and the inherent variability of plaque characteristics among individuals and clinical settings further complicate these challenges. Addressing these issues is crucial for improving the reliability and generalizability of machine learning-based plaque quantification using intraoral photography. Practical challenges, such as the costs associated with acquiring and maintaining necessary hardware and software, as well as the required training and expertise for clinicians, pose barriers to widespread implementation. To address these considerations, we propose an innovative protocol for dental cavity prediction using a Modified YOLO-based Deep Learning Model (MYoD-M), which aims to increase the reliability of the prediction mechanism. In our proposed model having two stages of implementation procedure, in primary we perform the super-pixilation based image enhancement with Gaussian-MRFi based segmentation. In stage 2, MYoD-Model is used to predict the dental cavity stages in four classes with boundary lines. Our proposed model outperformed the key performance indices with the overall accuracy nearly 94.5%.

articleTitle: Leveraging Explainable AI (XAI) Across Diverse Domains: IoT, Biomedicine, and Cyber security
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: This paper discusses the growing importance of Explainable AI (XAI), as it relates to making machine learning models more transparent and trustworthy in various applications and fields. In this regard, XAI addresses the need to understand to trust the most complex titles. In biomedicine, XAI assists clinicians in understanding the decisions made by machine learning-based models in the course of diagnosis, thus enabling improved patient management. In cyber security, it supports generating and situating further actions once the AI has flagged an anomaly, which increases overall security. In the Internet of Things (IoT), XAI assists in identifying the integrity of the system by spotting irregularities in the uniformity of interactions from various sources. In particular, this research investigates core XAI methods including but not limited to LIME, SHAP, and the application of interpretable models in decision-making, particularly focusing on decision trees and their implementation in practice in these fields. A comparative evaluation of XAI strategies is also presented to provide the information that is useful about implementation. Hence providing with an adequate theoretical basis for XAI, as well as practical recommendations on incorporating explain ability into the models of AI for biomedicine, cyber security, and IoT.

articleTitle: Development of an Intent-Based University Chatbot Using Supervised Learning and NLP Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: In the current digital age, chatbots have emerged as essential tools for enhancing communication and providing instant assistance in universities, addressing diverse information needs of students, alumni, and external stakeholders. This paper introduces an intent-based chatbot developed using machine learning techniques, particularly a deep learning feed-forward neural network model. Existing systems often lack accuracy and contextual relevance, resulting in unsatisfactory user experiences. Our approach utilizes a predefined dataset of user intents, applies tokenization and lemmatization, and feeds the processed data into a robustly designed neural network to ensure high accuracy and relevance. This chatbot significantly enhances communication efficiency within university settings and holds promise as an essential tool for fostering engagement among students and other stakeholders.

articleTitle: AI and IoT-Driven Crop Management System for Precision Agriculture and Optimized Resource Utilization
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: The integration of Artificial intelligence (AI) and Internet of Things (IoT) for precision agriculture is considered to be a greatest milestone. Traditional agriculture involves manual observation and real-time decision for the management of crops and resources. Precision agriculture integrates technologies to automate these processes and improve efficiency. IoT is used to collect the real-time data. AI is used in the interpretation of the data from IoT and making decisions based on certain conditions and gives actionable insights. Optimization of resources is one other crucial task that needs to be automated to compete with rising global challenges like population growth, global warming etc. The Novelty of this research lies in the integration of AI and IoT to collect real-time data and analyse it to take necessary actions towards crops and resources. The system would be able to adapt dynamically to counter the changes in environment, weather patterns and health of the crop. The Machine Learning models helps to make accurate decisions based on the parameters. The high cost and maintenance of the IoT devices AI would be a huge challenge for wide spread adoption by farmers who are practicing agriculture at a small scale. To power these devices, constant electricity and high speed internet is required which is a challenge in remote areas. Farmers should be taught these new technologies so that they can use it more efficiently. Thus training the farmers and making them gain the necessary skills is another challenge. The objective of this research is to develop an AI – IoT – driven system that effectively monitors the crops in real time and helps in the optimization of resources leading to high yield and quality of the crops. The system automates the process of decision making and provide actionable insights based on real-time data. All the data and alerts are provided to the framer through a mobile application or a web application with alerts and recommendations.

articleTitle: Elevate - An Intelligent Companion for Mental Wellness
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: Mental health is an emerging worldwide concern, with individuals from various backgrounds facing barriers in receiving professional care due to economic constraints, social stigma, and limited availability. Elevate is a virtual companion designed to bridge this gap by providing cost-free personalized, and easily accessible mental health care through sophisticated natural language processing (NLP) and sentiment analysis through Google’s Gemini API. The earlier version of Elevate, primarily catered to students, Elevate has now been designed to serve a wider audience. The system is equipped with a secure user-authentication mechanism that enables personalized interactions and specific support. With the multitab approach and interactive sidebar for chat history, users have ease of access to old conversations, thus enhancing usability and engagement. A well-structured database and robust backend architecture ensure efficient data management while upholding the highest privacy standards. Through the use of artificial intelligence to provide real-time emotional support, motivational material, personalized roadmaps, and stress management strategies, Elevate has emerged as an effective and scalable solution to mental health. In this research, the technical innovation, user experience improvements, and metrics of evaluation that make Elevate an end-to-end AI-driven companion to mental well-being are presented.

articleTitle: Dynamic AI Collaboration Frameworks Using Real-Time Multimodal Feedback Loops for Complex Task Automation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: AI solutions are introduced in various complex, unstructured and perpetually evolving contexts, wherein multiple agents are often needed to cooperate in order to accomplish a given set of objectives. In such environment, flexibility is crucial because such systems are required to alter their operation in accordance with changes occurring in the environment. However, there are problems associated with traditional multi-agent systems to provide the wanted level of flexibility in order to react promptly to the constantly changing environment and handle a variety of sensory inputs. This paper describes a new Dynamic AI Collaboration Framework to address these issues by incorporating multi-modal feedback from vision, audio and text, haptic feedback streams. This framework is composed by a Dynamic Role Assigner based on reinforcement learning that will assign the roles of the agents according to the variations of the environment. This can be done to a much larger extent than in the earlier examples, and flexible adaptive AI agents can alter their roles without any problems according to their assessment of the ongoing task and its environment. This paper also presents an evaluation of the effectiveness of the proposed framework in a number of simulated disaster-response scenarios where our approach proves to be 25% more efficient and 40% more dynamic as compared to the conventional static role allocation based approaches. The findings show that adopting remote multimodal feedback as well as dynamic role allocation strengthen synergistic interactions among AI participants and guarantee optimised performance in critical, transient situations. In this work numerous applications are presented for dynamic AI systems for example in disaster response and industrial automation, in collaborative creative processes and health care showing that dynamic systems have a variety of uses in different fields.

articleTitle: Advance Threat Detection Using Machine Learning Techniques With Ssh Honeypot An Integrated Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: Cybersecurity threats have become increasingly sophisticated, with attackers frequently targeting SSH services to gain unauthorized access to critical systems. Traditional security measures often fall short in identifying and mitigating these advanced attacks. This project's primary goal is to create an SSH honeypot which includes machine learning methods to improve the identification and examination of harmful activity. This issue is crucial to solve because current security solutions cannot adapt to and identify novel attack patterns in real-time dynamically. The gaps in existing work include the limited use of machine learning for real-time analysis of honeypot data and the need for more sophisticated feature extraction methods to improve detection accuracy. To address these gaps, we deploy the Cowrie SSH honeypot to collect detailed logs of attack attempts. In this we are using Kaggle honeypot dataset and then preprocess this data, extract relevant features, and label data into malicious and benign, after that we apply machine learning models to identify among categorize harmful activity, including Random Forest, LightGBM, SVM, XGBoost, Naive Bayes, and decision trees. The enhanced precision along with promptness of attack detection, which offers a proactive defense mechanism against changing cyberthreats, are the project's main contributions. This approach transforms raw security data into actionable intelligence, enhancing the overall cybersecurity posture.

articleTitle: HydroSavvy: Modernizing Agriculture with Intelligent Irrigation Solutions Using IoT
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: This research introduces a new term, Hydro-Savvy. It is an innovative, intelligent irrigation system that optimizes water application and increases crop yields using the Internet of Things, Artificial Intelligence, and advanced sensors. Among the features include the mesh network of soil moisture sensors to obtain real-time data on scheduling irrigation, flow meters that offer insight into water usage, and leak detection to monitor the pump and valves in order not to waste water. It is accessible even where the internet might be small, and it uses solar panels with a battery backup to work 24/7. The multilingual AI mobile application supports voice commands and assists in real-time water consumption tracking, maintaining logs of irrigation activities, efficiency reports, and guidelines for saving water. The system integrates with the weather API, thus preventing drought irrigation, while machine learning models predict the likelihood of future irrigations as required based on data about weather, soil, and crops. The backend coding is Node.js, with data stored on Google Cloud and Firebase. This research exemplifies the potential for IoT and AI to revolutionize water management toward sustainability and better agricultural productivity.

articleTitle: Analysis of Epithelial Ovarian Cancer Subtypes Classification on Histopathological Images Using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: Epithelial ovarian cancer is an aggressive form of gynecologic malignancy that significantly contributes to morbidity and mortality rates among women globally. Effective diagnosis and classification of its subtypes such as High Grade Serous Carcinoma (HGSC), Clear Cell Ovarian Carcinoma (CC), Endometrioid Carcinoma (EC), Low Grade Serous Carcinoma (LGSC), and Mucinous Carcinoma (MC) are crucial for accurate treatment planning and prognosis. This study employs advanced deep learning techniques to automate the classification and analysis of these subtypes using histopathology images. The preprocessing steps involve grayscale conversion, edge detection, histogram equalization, and Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) to improve image quality and maintain consistency during feature extraction. To achieve effective classification, multiple deep learning models are evaluated, including a modified Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), VGG16, ResNet, and DenseNet. These architectures are further integrated with techniques for precise tumor region localization. A thorough accuracy assessment is conducted to determine the most effective model for subtype classification. This research aims to provide a scalable and reliable framework for diagnostic support, enhancing patient care by facilitating personalized treatment strategies through innovative deep learning approaches.

articleTitle: Sensing an Activated Mobile Phone by using Transmitted Signals
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: The changes that have taken place over the centuries have led to the better development of science and technology, but have also aroused many scammers. Some examples of technologies that have evolved in recent years include: there is online transactions, internet banking, sports and other entertainment. Especially in education during the pandemic (COVID-19). In this situation, the use of mobile phones was compulsory. After the pandemic, students continued to attend school, college, and resume real life, but kept their mobile phones in the facility. For example, students in a classroom or examination room may seek to communicate informally with those outside the hall for whatever purpose. Mobile phone activity is identified by the presence of a transmitted signal. It is based on radio frequency (RF) principles. Developing and implementing a mobile phone detector is part of our project. This portable gadget will identify a cell phone that is also in silent mode (an active cell phone). This detector is designed to detect within a radius of 1.5 meters

articleTitle: Enhancing User Interaction in Digital Financial Systems Using AI-Driven Front-End Technologies: A Personalised Response Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: This study highlights the rapid advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML), which have transformed the financial sector by enhancing personalised user interactions and customer engagement. An innovative AI-driven framework was proposed to deliver real-time, context-aware, and highly personalised responses for Digital Banking users. The system architecture employs advanced ML models, natural language processing (NLP) techniques, and modern front-end technologies such as React and GraphQL to address the challenges related to data silos, computational demand, and data privacy. ML models such as user segmentation, recommendation, and NLP models work together to analyse user behaviour, predict needs, and generate human-like responses. Utilising React, GraphQL subscriptions, and Edge AI, the front-end layer ensures a seamless and responsive user experience. The experimental results showed a 120% increase in click-through rates, a 180% increase in follow-up actions, and a 70% reduction in average response time, demonstrating significant improvements in user engagement. User satisfaction, measured by the Net Promoter Score, was significantly higher for the personalised system (8.5) than for the traditional system (5.2). The proposed methodology lays the foundation for an agile trust-based financial environment. Future enhancements will focus on explainable AI, multimodal interactions, and blockchain integration to boost transparency, engagement, and data privacy.

articleTitle: Exploring Zero-Shot Learning in Natural Language Processing for Cross-Domain Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: The research assesses how three and two state-of-the-art pre-trained language models (PLMs) function alongside BERT and BioBERT while operating on various natural language processing (NLP) functions which incorporate sentiment analysis, text classification, entity recognition and cross-domain sentiment classification. BERT and BioBERT achieve superior performance than all other models by delivering optimal accuracy ratings together with high precision and recall while obtaining the highest F1-score across all tasks. The generalization ability of BERT enables it to maintain top performance across four different domains which include product reviews, movie reviews, social media content and news articles. BioBERT demonstrates particular effectiveness when handling biomedical Natural Language Processing applications. The model performance of T5 matches BERT although BERT demonstrates better outcomes in specific tasks. RoBERTa together with GPT-2 achieves moderate success in particular use cases but consistently performs below the current best NLP models. BERT-based models demonstrate superior performance in various NLP applications which demonstrates their strength in dealing with complicated operations yet researchers need to investigate RoBERTa and GPT-2 specifically within individual domains to achieve superior outcomes.

articleTitle: AutoMediVision:A Deep Learning System for Accurate Pharmaceutical pill identification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: The goal of this project is to build a high performance system that offers prediction of pill information from images, the pill name, medical use and recommended dosage by using MobileNet which is a lightweight and efficient deep learning model. This system serves as an important tool for healthcare professionals and patients as it offers a means of reducing risk because of the large number of medications out there. For this task, MobileNet was chosen for its high accuracy and good balance between computational efficiency and high accuracy, and hence can be deployed on mobile devices. Having trained the model on a wide variety of pills with class wise annotations, it generalized well for diverse pills. The output of the system is the pill name, primary medical indications and common dosage instructions that help in safer medication management by supporting healthcare providers in providing better care and patient safety.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review of Real-Time Sign Language Interpretation Using Various Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: Real-time Sign Language interpretation is among the fastest-growing fields that can potentially minimize the communication gap between deaf people and the hearing population and prepare the ground for inclusivity and accessibility throughout social, educational, and professional contexts. The review discusses the development of technologies for sign languages interpretation in real time, having the main emphasis that have to be met such as high interpretation accuracy, low latency, and computational efficiency. This review methodology, which compared machine learning and deep learning algorithms and discussed different model architectures, analyzed the trends and emerging methodologies that have shaped the current state of the field and identified significant gaps in the literature. In particular, the tendency is such that the multimodality involving hand, face, and body movement participation is becoming increasingly more effective; the pre-trained models get adapted to perform sign language tasks. Most importantly, diversity in datasets promotes model robustness across languages and dialects. A bit further, practical problems are discussed with real-time interpretation deployment on mobile devices and other resource-limited platforms. The following review is designed to point out the likely best directions for future research and development that would generalize, through the advancement of real time sign language interpretation, to become an accessible and reliable technology for everyday use.

articleTitle: YOLOv8-Based Real-Time System for Breed and Disease Detection in Birds to Enhance Health Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: As the popularity of pet birds continues to grow, there is an increasing demand for advanced health monitoring systems that can provide timely and accurate care. Conventional methods of bird health monitoring rely heavily on manual observation, which can be subjective, error-prone, and reactive rather than proactive. This project proposes an automated system utilizing the YOLOv8 deep learning model to detect bird breeds and identify symptoms of diseases in real-time. By leveraging a large and diverse dataset, this system uses computer vision to continuously monitor birds, enabling early disease detection through high-speed video processing. The system is designed to send alerts to pet owners and veterinarians at the first signs of health issues, facilitating timely interventions and improving overall health outcomes. The inclusion of a feedback loop allows the model to continuously improve its accuracy through user input and retraining with new data. This methodology provides a scalable and adaptable solution for pet bird care, reducing dependence on physical examinations and providing comprehensive monitoring 24 hours a day. The project highlights substantive advances in real-time animal care technology with potential applications across a wide bird species and environmental spectrum.

articleTitle: Enhancing Brain Tumor Diagnosis: A Hybrid Machine Learning Model with PCA and SHAP for Interpretability
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: To enhance patient prognosis, identifying and diagnosing brain tumors at an early stage are significantly important. For this purpose, we present a hybrid machine learning based framework for brain tumor identification which utilizes principal component analysis (PCA), support vector classifiers (SHC), and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) for optimal performance and interpretability. In medical imaging data, the degree of complexity and variety is so high that in order to improve efficiency and minimize overfitting, it is more reasonable to employ dimensions reduction techniques which as support vector classifiers (SVC) PCA to SVC is used in Shapley to increase computation speed without loss of important diagnostic features. Because of its robustness to high-dimensional data and ability to provide clear decision boundaries, SVC is used as the primary classifier, while logistic regression is employed as the benchmark for comparison. To enhance the explainability of machine learning healthcare models, SHAP is used to understand the role different predictors play which will in turn increase clinicians trust in the model. The approach is aimed to the Brain Tumor MRI Dataset at Kaggle, where the model has claimed to have outperformed others. The model outperforms the baseline model in terms of accuracy, precision and recall when identifying cases with and without a brain tumor. Through the integration of dimensionality reduction and interpretable machine learning techniques, we not only achieve accurate diagnostic results, but also address the issue of reconciling sophisticated algorithmic models with clinical use. This approach serves as a potential real-time brain tumor diagnosis and patient management tool.

articleTitle: SmartShield: Harnessing Code Extraction and ML for Next-Gen Malware Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: The rapid proliferation of Android applications has led to an increased prevalence of malware, posing significant security risks to users and devices. This research presents a novel Hybrid Model for Android malware detection, integrating multiple machine learning algorithms to enhance accuracy and robustness. The methodology involves the systematic collection of a comprehensive dataset, extraction of critical features using the Code Extraction Principle (CEP), and the evaluation of various models including SVM, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, and others. The proposed Hybrid Model significantly outperforms these models, achieving an accuracy of 97.81%, with precision and recall rates of 96.72% and 95.89%, respectively. This model’s superior performance is attributed to the effective combination of different algorithms, optimizing feature extraction, and the robust handling of both benign and malicious applications. The model’s robustness against evasion techniques further underscores its potential as a reliable tool in Android malware detection. The results indicate that the proposed Hybrid Model is highly effective in minimizing both false positives and false negatives, offering a promising solution for enhancing mobile security. The findings of this research contribute to the development of more secure and efficient malware detection systems, addressing the evolving challenges in mobile cybersecurity.

articleTitle: Vehiguard Transfer Learning-Driven Quantum PSO-LSTM for Automotive Cyber Security
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: Quantum-Inspired Particle Swarm Optimization (QPSO) has emerged as a powerful optimization technique that enhances hyper parameter tuning and convergence efficiency in machine learning models. In the context of vehicular network security, integrating QPSO with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks and Transfer Learning offers a robust framework for detecting cyber threats in dynamic vehicular environments. Traditional anomaly detection mechanisms often struggle with real-time adaptability, leading to reduced detection accuracy and delayed response to evolving attack vectors. The proposed VehiGuard framework leverages QPSO to optimize hyper parameters efficiently, improving LSTM’s ability to detect anomalies in vehicular data streams. Transfer learning further enhances model adaptability by utilizing pre-trained models from related domains, significantly reducing the need for extensive labelled datasets while maintaining high detection accuracy. This hybrid approach ensures a scalable and computationally efficient solution for vehicular cyber security. Empirical evaluations conducted on widely used vehicular datasets demonstrate that VehiGuard outperforms conventional models in terms of detection accuracy, computational efficiency, and robustness against diverse attack vectors. The results highlight the potential of integrating quantum-inspired optimization with deep learning and knowledge transfer to secure autonomous vehicles and IoT-enabled transportation systems. By addressing critical challenges in vehicular network security, VehiGuard contributes to the development of more resilient and adaptive intelligent transportation systems.

articleTitle: Enhanced Deep Learning Approaches For Brain Tumor Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: Determining whether the brain contains a tumor in its initial stages leads to effective medical intervention for boosting patient survival. This study explores a new technique of the classification of brain tumors involving a combination of Convolutional Neural Networks and Support Vector Machines, where the system makes differential diagnosis using MRI scans against three types of tumors; Glioma, Meningioma, and Pituitary. To provide accurate analysis based on patterns, CNNs for feature extraction and SVM to classify images are used. Since the preprocessing techniques used ensure perfection in accuracy, partial differential equations are used for enhanced image enhancement and Gray-Level Co-occurrence Matrix, thereby contributing to texture analysis. Building the model with Tensor Flow on GoogleNet architecture optimized towards high performance is considered optimal. The evaluation results show that the system works well, and the system is able to achieve a high accuracy rate on the medical datasets. The proposed framework offers a reliable and efficient tool for assisting medical professionals in early diagnosis, thereby contributing to better treatment planning.

articleTitle: Integrating Artificial Intelligence with Cloud Platforms to Optimize Performance, Scalability, and Reliability in Distributed Computing Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: This non-stop advancement of distributed computing systems due to the necessity of achieving big data processing for real-time data processing and high work complexity requires better solutions for enhancing high-performance, scalability, and reliability. This study focuses on the interaction between AI and Cloud Computing, to improve the performance of Distributed Systems. It is the hope of this paper that with the use of AI-adaptive algorithms and machine learning, resource distribution can be optimized, system constraints can be forecasted with + precision, and summaries can be made fault resilient across various computational platforms. The focus techniques are reinforcement learning for dynamic resource management, genetic algorithms for load distribution, and federated learning for enhanced data confidentiality and distributed model training. Further, workload prediction is done using time-series based or machine-learning based predictive Analytics, and deep learning-based anomaly detection for health monitoring and autoencoder for fault diagnosis. Container orchestration and micro services architecture has been implemented in the proposed framework for achieving flexibility and scalability in multi-cloud and hybrid cloud systems. The experimental results show the effectiveness of the proposed implementation to enhance the system performance, scalability and reliability and thus signaling a new dawn for AI based solutions in distributed computing systems.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Model for Video-Based Human Fall Detection Using CRNN and EfficientNet
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: People as they age, activities can become increasingly difficult, and they may require more assistance to carry out their routine tasks. This is because of physical, mental, and cognitive limitations that can affect their ability to perform daily activities. Social connections are critical to both mental and physical health. When seniors are lonely, they can experience real physical symptoms. Their blood pressure drops too much when they get up from sitting or lying down, they have balance and gait issues and they are prone to fainting and falling because of age-related muscle loss. It is generally considered as the sign of declining physical strength, balance issues, or other health-related concerns that require professional attention. As in some cases, they might require immediate actions to be taken due to potential for serious consequences. Continues monitoring, hospitalization might lead to long term disabilities and health care cost. This paper addresses this problem by introducing Deep Learning-Based Video-Based Human Fall Detection which plays a crucial part in promoting immediate attention and identification of falls, particularly among elderly individuals, by leveraging technology to monitor and respond quickly to such events. This serves as an effective solution to ensure immediate intervention in case of emergencies. Deep learning techniques are utilized to monitor an individual's physical appearance in real-time for fall detection. An alert is triggered if the person collapses or exhibits any significant deviation from their normal posture. The pre-processing phase begins with the application of a Gaussian filter to reduce noise, followed by feature extraction using the EfficientNet model for accurate analysis. Convolutional neural networks (CNN) and recurrent neural networks (RNN) are combined in the detection process to efficiently analyse temporal and spatial features from live video. Upon detecting a fall, an alert is promptly sent to the registered user's contact number via the Twilio API, ensuring timely intervention.

articleTitle: AI Deep Learning Methods for Segmenting 3D-Brain Tumors Images using U-Net
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: Deep learning approaches have transformed medical image segmentation, particularly for the automatic separation of brain tumours in pre-operative MRI scans. This study suggests a better U-Net design to fix the problems with current ones, like not splitting edge features enough, not getting location information well, and using feature details too many times without changing them, which are all problems with older models. The suggested model combines a serial encoding-decoding method with a hybrid dilated convolution module. It also includes inter-module concatenations to improve the accuracy of segmentation. To improve classification and segmentation performance, a new loss function that prioritizes difficult-to-segment data is also developed. The BraTS dataset, which includes MRI images of different types (T1, T1c, T2, and FLAIR) found in three different parts of brain tumors—enhanced tumor (EST), tumor core (TC), and entire tumor (WT)—was used to test how well the model worked. The segmentation results are judged using metrics such as dice, an IOU, Hausdorff95, and PA among ASD. These show that the suggested model consistently works better than current methods. Visual comparisons provide additional confirmation of its capacity to capture more detailed tumour features and generate results that are more accurate. The results show that the model is very good at semantic segmentation, which could have effects on clinical workflows like therapy planning. They also show that the model can be used to help with brain tumor research for both diagnosis and treatment. The proposed model achieved superior segmentation performance with an mIoU of 89.45%, MPA of 92.35%, precision of 95.98%, and Dice of 94.01%. These results demonstrate its strong capability in accurately segmenting brain tumours, outperforming existing methods.

articleTitle: Synergizing Quantum Cryptography and Post-Quantum Cryptography: A New Era of Ultra-Secure Data Transmission
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: Quantum Cryptography (QC) is a newer method of ultra-secure key transmission that relies more on Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocols. On the contrary, Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) is concerned about the high-security encryption of data that uses algorithms like the Kyber algorithm. However, both face unique challenges: QC requires costly QKD hardware, offers limited scalability due to point-to-point communication, and is vulnerable to physical attacks like side-channel and denial-of-service exploits, while PQC is resource-intensive, prone to latency issues, and faces uncertainties regarding future quantum algorithms that may compromise its security. Some challenges that QC and PQC face are overcome by merging both of them for the hybrid approach. This review explores synergy between QC and PQC, proposing a hybrid solution for combining QKD-based secure key exchange with the PQC quantum-resistant encryption capability. This integration delivers robust, future-proof communication with protection against both classical and quantum threats.

articleTitle: InsightQA: Descriptive Question and Answer Generation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: Present research largely concentrates on the generation and evaluation of objective-type questions, with significantly less focus on automating the creation of subjective questions and answers. As the demand for contextually relevant question answer generation grows, the manual task of setting of subjective question papers and assessment of their descriptive responses becomes increasingly burdensome and time-consuming. As a consequence of this, the educators are unable to dedicate time to more crucial tasks of strategic and engaging educational activities. Also, the existing data sets for descriptive question answer pairs contain very short length answers such as answer in two to three words or very short single sentence answers. To tackle these challenges, we have created our own data set labelled DescQA which includes question answer pairs from diverse educational domains and an Advanced Language Model (ALM) that automates the generation of contextually appropriate descriptive questions and answers. Utilizing cutting-edge natural language processing (NLP) techniques and a diverse dataset specifically designed for this purpose, our model accurately interprets educational materials to produce contextually relevant descriptive questions and answers. This initiative aims to reduce the workload on paper setters, enabling them to prioritize personalized instruction and student engagement. By generating more contextually relevant descriptive questions and answers, the ALM aspires to improve the learning experience for both educators and learners.

articleTitle: A Decision Tree Model-Based Classification of Abnormal Red Blood Cells
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: The diagnosis of a number of hematological illnesses depends on the ability to recognize and categorize aberrant red blood cells (RBCs). Furthermore, blood is composed of several components, namely platelets, plasma, red blood cells, white blood cells, etc. A red blood cell abnormalities can be classified by size (exocytosis), shape (poikilocytosis), color, or even the existence of bodies for inclusion. Finding these variations in red blood cell morphologies is important for one's well-being as it might reveal whether or not the blood is in good condition. To categorize aberrant red blood cell morphologies, hematologists, pathologists, and medical technicians often employed a manually using a microscope technique. This approach is challenging and prone to human mistake. To address this problem, a variety of strategies were used, including as convolutional neural networks for detection, machine learning-based classification, and image processing techniques. One machine-learning classification method is the Decision-Tree methodology. As a result, the system found and identified ten aberrant red blood cells. Hospital patients have already provided the images utilized in the system. The image was modified and categorized by the computer. The names of the aberrant red blood cells that the system detected in the picture are displayed in the results. The algorithm classified aberrant RBCs with a precision of 94.5% and recall of 93.2%, according to the results. The suggested decision tree technique provides an easy-to-use and effective method for automatically classifying aberrant red blood cells. In clinical contexts, it may help diagnose hematological problems and increase the effectiveness of blood analysis.

articleTitle: Unlocking the Power of UPI: A Machine Learning Journey through Digital Payment and data visualization models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: This paper investigates the integration of Computational Linguistics techniques and Intelligent Data Analysis models to enhance customer satisfaction within the Seamless Payment Platform framework in digital payments. By analyzing customer interactions and feedback, the study aims to uncover insights that improve the user experience and operational efficiency of the All-in-One Payment Interface. The research employs advanced data visualization methods to illustrate the impact of Predictive Analytics on understanding user sentiments and preferences, ultimately contributing to a more effective and satisfying digital payment experience. rewrite with Computational Linguistics with Data visualization framework

articleTitle: The Face Recognition Attendance System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: The Face Recognition Attendance System is an innovative solution developed to automate and make attendance tracking much easier in educational institutions and workplaces. The system recognizes people with face recognition efficiently using Python, Flask, OpenCV, and Firebase, and records attendance real-time. Users can upload images to the database for easy face matching at the time of attendance checking, thus maintaining accuracy and eliminating errors caused by a human eye. Teachers can access the records of attendance with secure login. Multi-class management is supported and this system is integrated with Firebase to enable efficient storage and retrieval of data. Use of advanced algorithms like DeepFace and FaceNet will support robust face detection, alignment, and recognition. It comes with high flexibility due to real-time updations and user-friendliness along with open-source adaptability, and hence, this system is based on leading-edge machine learning and computer vision technologies together that makes it an effective and reliable alternative to conventional attendance methods, hence looking for improvement in productivity and accountability.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Collaboration: HoloSync 5G’s Real-Time Holographic Magic
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: The HoloSync 5G Hybrid Model represents a groundbreaking solution for real-time holographic communication, integrating 5G infrastructure, advanced machine learning techniques, and dynamic compression algorithms. This model designed to address the challenges of high latency, bandwidth constraints, and rendering inconsistencies in global remote collaboration. The system leverages Multi-Access Edge Computing (MEC) for low-latency data processing, while adaptive encoding and decoding ensure seamless data transmission. Experimental results demonstrate a 44% reduction in latency and a 41% improvement in bandwidth utilization compared to baseline systems. Rendering fidelity significantly enhanced, with a 9.41% increase in SSIM (0.93) and 11.78% improvement in PSNR (42.7 dB). User satisfaction ratings average 4.8/5, reflecting the intuitive design and clarity of the holographic experience. Scalability testing confirmed consistent performance, even in sessions with up to 50 users. These results validate the HoloSync model as a robust and efficient platform for applications such as telemedicine, remote education, and industrial collaboration. The study concludes with promising insights into the potential of hybrid intelligence and 5G advancements to redefine real-time holographic communication.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of YOLOv8 and EfficientDet for Object Detection in Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: Object detection is the essential role in autonomous driving. This research examining two object detection models YOLOv8, which is effectively use for its real time performance and EfficientDet is well known for its efficiency with strong reliability. Because to its speed and reliability, YOLOv8 is mostly used in autonomous vehicles. EfficientDet is a strong rival provides better reliability, efficiency and ability of process for various self driving applications, despite being less popular for object detection tasks. This article investigate both models on variety of datasets, emphasizing the efficiency in terms of precision, recall and inference speed. Based on findings, EfficientDet is an ideal option for object identification tasks where accuracy is crucial as it higher sucess YOLOv8 in real time applications as well as outperforming it in terms of accuracy and material efficiency. Even with limited application, EfficientDet offers a lot of potential for potential implementation that require high accuracy object detection.

articleTitle: Automating Fake News Detection and Content Moderation Using Machine Learning: A Comprehensive Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: Fake news and toxic online content proliferate across digital platforms, causing harm to the trust of the social structure. In this context, this study focuses on using machine learning techniques to help solve such problems by using automated detection and moderation systems. We will present a framework that combines advanced natural language processing (NLP) methods with supervised learning algorithms to detect misinformation and inappropriate content in various domains. Training and validation rely on publicly available datasets, so model performance can be fully assessed. The paper highlights a comprehensive study on feature extraction, such as sentiment analysis, contextual embedding, and linguistic patterns, and also shows a scalable architecture for real-time content evaluation. The experiments reveal that the developed system correctly identifies fake news from reliable information and can detect violative activities concerning community guidelines. It addresses explainability and the importance of mitigating biases within machine learning models that enhance the prospects for fairness and transparency. Its findings also allow actionable contributions to improved automated content moderation systems toward the more safety-oriented digital ecosystem.

articleTitle: Next-Gen Penetration Testing: AI, Automation & Beyond
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: As the digital frontier expands, so does the complexity of cyber threats, necessitating a shift in penetration testing practices. This paper explores the evolution from traditional methods to innovative approaches driven by artificial intelligence (AI), quantum computing, and crowd− sourcing. AI enhances penetration testing by improving speed and precision, enabling the simulation of adaptive attackers and uncovering vulnerabilities that might go unnoticed by conventional methods. Quantum computing, while promising to accelerate testing, also introduces challenges by threatening existing cryptographic defenses, pushing the need for quantum−resistant encryption. Crowdsourced penetration testing leverages the collective expertise of ethical hackers to identify vulnerabilities that automated tools may miss, providing a more thorough and diverse assessment. By integrating these emerging technologies with traditional strategies, the paper envisions a more dynamic, proactive approach to cybersecurity. This evolution will position penetration testing as a cornerstone of cyber resilience, enabling organizations to stay ahead of sophisticated threats.

articleTitle: Exploring Mechanistic Interpretability in Large Language Models: Challenges, Approaches, and Insights
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have significantly enhanced their performance across a wide array of tasks. However, the lack of interpretability has become a critical concern, particularly as these models grow in size and complexity. Mechanistic interpretability seeks to uncover the internal workings of neural networks, offering valuable insights into their decision-making processes, biases, and potential safety risks. This survey delves into the emerging field of mechanistic interpretability for LLMs, emphasizing the need to reverse-engineer these models to ensure ethical and reliable AI systems. We provide a comprehensive examination of key techniques, including feature representation, circuit analysis, and causal intervention methods. The survey also discusses challenges such as polysemanticity and superposition, which complicate the understanding of individual model components. By exploring these frontiers, the paper highlights the importance of mechanistic interpretability in improving model transparency, robustness, and alignment with human values, while identifying open challenges in the field.

articleTitle: Academic Temporal Pattern Mining for Enhanced Student Performance Prediction: A Hybrid Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: Predicting student academic performance effectively remains challenging due to the dynamic nature of learning behavior and the complex interplay of factors affecting student success. This paper introduces Academic Temporal Pattern Mining (ATPM), a novel approach that identifies critical time-based patterns in student academic behavior to enhance performance prediction accuracy. Unlike traditional methods that rely on static snapshots of student data, our approach analyzes sequential patterns in study habits, submission timings, and performance trends. Using a UCI Student Performance Dataset of 1,000 undergraduates, we demonstrate that temporal patterns such as assignment submission sequences and grade progression provide crucial predictive insights. Our hybrid model, combining Random Forest for feature stability and XGBoost for capturing non-linear relationships, achieves an accuracy of 87%, representing a 15% improvement over conventional regression-based methods. Moreover, we rigorously evaluate the statistical significance of these gains (p < 0.05) and show an 80% precision threshold for early warning up to three assessment cycles before final grades. This research contributes to educational data mining by offering a practical and scalable framework for temporal pattern analysis that leverages readily available academic data for timely, actionable interventions.

articleTitle: Strategic Pricing in Global Smartphone Ecosystem-Game Theoretic Insights for Digital Platform Services Supply Chain
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: The study examines pricing strategies of iOS and Android within the global smartphone ecosystem by using a Prisoner's Dilemma Model. It incorporates global market share trends and application store revenues to calculate the pay-off for the game model. The model evaluates average revenue per device under each strategic interaction to analyze the impact of such pricing on digital platform services supply chain. It also incorporates comparative static analysis; supervised learning-based simulation and regression forecasts; K-Means Clustering to scrutinize robustness and real-world applicability of the research. The findings highlight the importance of co-operative strategies among the players to maintain a stable smartphone ecosystem globally. Thus, this research tries to provide insights for businesses, investors and academicians on improving supply chain resilience while promoting market growth for the digital platform services.

articleTitle: HybridBoost Ensemble Model for Enhanced Cervical Cancer Detection: A Multi-Stage Feature Optimization Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: Early cervical cancer diagnosis drastically improves treatment efficacy, requiring sensitive and effective models for diagnostics. This research offers a new HybridBoost Ensemble Model that integrates cutting-edge preprocessing techniques, feature extraction, feature selection, and classification to boost detection efficiency. The proposed preprocessing pipeline contains TriPhase Augmentation with normalization, grayscale trans- formation, and flipping, in combination with Pentamorphic Transformation through brightness, contrast enhancement, edge detection, Gaussian blur, and rotation to optimize image quality. This unified histogram of oriented gradients (HOG), local binary pattern (LBP), Scale-Invariant Feature Transform (SIFT), and Gabor filters method, enhanced gradient-texture fusion (EGTF), helps to represent feature exhaustively. To reduce the features with dimension reduction and preserve vital information, this uses a Genetic Algorithm (GA) and PCA. The HybridBoost Ensemble Model is a union of logistic regression, random forest, support vector machines, KNN, Adaboost, and GradientBoost classifier, optimized through GridSearchCV. The ensemble ap- proach augments bagging, boosting, stacking, and voting to improve generalization and minimize overfitting. Experimental evaluations exhibit substantial performance improvements over baseline methods measured by various performance metrics.. The proposed approach is an effective, automated, and scalable solution for early cervical cancer detection.

articleTitle: Blockchain in Supply Chain Management, Remittance and Sports Industry
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: The analysis of blockchain technology demonstrates significant potential in transforming remittance services, sports, and sustainable supply chains. Its ability to address challenges such as expensive and slow cross border payment processes in remittance services ensures secure and cost effective peer to peer transactions. In sports, blockchain enhances operational efficiency, promotes fan engagement through tokenized assets, and enables transparent smart contract management. For sustainable supply chains, it tackles critical issues such as traceability, fraud mitigation, and real time data sharing, ensuring secure tracking and accountability across complex systems. Additionally, blockchain fosters decentralized ecosystems, reducing dependency on intermediaries while enhancing operational resilience. Its robust security framework further mitigates risks associated with data breaches and unauthorized access, making it indispensable for industries requiring transparency, trust, and efficiency. The study also explores the role of smart contracts in automating processes, minimizing errors, and streamlining operations across diverse applications.

articleTitle: A Data-Driven Approach to Habit Prediction: Computational Modeling and Emotion Analytics
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: This paper introduces a computational model for gathering data from diverse sources to improve both group and individual communication by integrating visual and audio inputs, emotional sensitivity metrics, and performance evaluations. The ET model analyzes complex data patterns and draws insights into the emotional response using emotional level tokens. The proposed approach will help organizations develop decision-support software to integrate human-data interaction into business processes, which in turn accelerates decision-making and offers a competitive advantage by using emotional analysis to produce actionable business knowledge.

articleTitle: Analysis and Automation of Pipe leakage deduction using Artificial intelligence and machine learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: The DNN-based water leakage detection system project has introduced an innovative approach to identify leakages in water distribution networks using Deep Neural Networks (DNNs). Traditional methods for detecting leaks often depend on manual inspection or costly sensor networks, which may not scalable or cost-effective. In contrast, this project applies the power of DNNs to automatically scrutinize audio data captured by microphones and detect leaks in real-time. The system operates by training a DNN model on a dataset of audio recordings containing both normal pipeline sounds and leak-related abnormalities. The trained model is then put in place to incessantly monitor audio data from strategically placed microphones along the pipeline network. By analyzing the audio signals using the trained DNN, the system can accurately identify and localize potential leaks with high precision using DNNs for leak detection, the project presents several advantages, including improved accuracy, scalability, and cost-effectiveness. Further-more, the system’s capacity to work in real-time enables water utilities to proactively detect and address leaks before they amplify into larger issues, thus reducing water loss and minimizing environmental impact. In general, the DNN-based water leakage detection system project represents a noteworthy advancement in the field of leak detection, offering an innovative solution that merges machine learning with audio signal processing to ensure the integrity of water distribution networks.

articleTitle: Predictive Modelling of Micro-Reinforced Rubberized Concrete Using ANFIS
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: This study explores the performance of rubberized concrete with the inclusion of steel fibers through a neural network approach for the determination of its strength parameters. Rubberized concrete is made by partially replacing conventional aggregates with recycled rubber. The use of rubberized concrete reuses waste materials and improves some of the mechanical properties but typically at the reduction of compressive strength. To overcome this limitation, it introduces steel fibers to boost the strength and ductility of the materials. This research study investigates combine impacts of rubber particles and steel fibers on performance of concrete. A developed neural network model is adopted to predict the key parameters concerning compressive strength, flexural strength, and modulus of elasticity with variable ratios of rubber and steel fibers. The sample is trained on experimental data for a broad range of concrete mixes, thus allowing for good predictions and optimization of the material composition. Results showed that rubberized concrete with steel fibers could maintain adequate strength while offering improved flexibility and crack resistance, making it a viable alternative to conventional concrete in certain structural applications. This approach also showcases the potential of machine learning techniques in advancing sustainable construction materials.

articleTitle: Secure cloud storage for health care data: An integrity auditing protocol ensuring privacy and public verifiability
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: To enhance the privacy and security of cloud store age systems, this paper proposes a complete integrity audit protocol well adapted to healthcare data management needs. The proposed protocol's privacy-preserving digital forensic readiness mechanism can be utilized by healthcare organizations to safely manage and store individual patient information while being compliant with the law. This protocol features public auditability, which keeps confidentiality intact as third-party auditors can maintain data integrity without having access to the data. It is effective for systems whose data changes over time since it accommodates dynamic data operations to facilitate frequent modification, deletion, and updates. This protocol presents a robust foundation that maintains integrity, privacy, and forensic-readiness.

articleTitle: Current Trends in Smart Home Sensors for Blood Glucose and Fetal Heart Rate Monitoring: A Systematic Review
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: Conventional approaches and regular clinical visits are usually needed for monitoring blood glucose levels and foetal heart rates. The two most popular techniques for checking blood sugar levels are finger-prick tests and continuous glucose monitors (CGMs), which need under-the-skin sensor insertions. Similar to this, Doppler ultrasonography equipment or cardiotocography (CTG) machines are typically used for foetal heart rate (FHR) monitoring during pregnancy. These devices are typically large and require a clinical setting. These conventional techniques can be expensive, difficult, and uncomfortable, which lowers adherence and causes gaps in monitoring. This study suggests wearable belts as a novel, Non- invasive way to monitor the patient health at the home. The suggested system uses infrared (IR) sensors that are integrated into a wearable belt to assess blood glucose levels non-invasively. The use of polyurethane fabric as a barrier to keep sweat off the sensors, improving their accuracy and longevity, is a noteworthy innovation. By processing the sensor data and displaying the glucose readings in real time on an LCD panel, an Arduino microcontroller offers a convenient and approachable substitute for traditional techniques. The paper describes a wearable device that is built into a belt for foetal Heart Rate monitoring. It uses an ARDUINO Microcontroller and hr module to continually detect and measure foetal heart rate. An LCD screen shows the readings in real time, making it easy for pregnant moms to check the health of their foetus from home. By providing dependable, affordable alternatives to conventional techniques, these gadgets can prevent the need for recurrent clinical visits and promote proactive health care. The suggested techniques seek to enhance overall health outcomes by facilitating more convenient and accessible continual monitoring.

Author Keywords: Wearable health devices Sweat protection layer component

articleTitle: Comprehensive Assistive Language Model (CALM) for Neurodivergent Child Language Acquisition
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: The Comprehensive Assistance Language Model–CALM, is a Natural Language Processing framework designed to support consistent language acquisition in children and aid their phonetic, semantic, and syntactic understanding. The model is intentionally designed to engage the child through empathy, task simplification, age-appropriate adaptation and trait-based multimodality. Most neurodivergent children struggle with language acquisition through traditional learning methods and develop a language gap that continues to grow into their adolescence and adulthood. Timely intervention through immersive learning approaches can mitigate or prevent these challenges. CALM integrates two components-a prompt-tuned LLM and a trained transformer model. The inclusion of a user report prepared by the prompt-tuned LLM on traits, age, caretaker concerns and detected condition understanding, increases the response quality and the child’s learning engagement. Layering a transformer model for contextual refinement and grammar correction over the LLM-generated response ensures coherence and improves relevance in answering the child’s query. CALM uses emojis and graphics as part of the generated text to enhance visual learning and also has the option of speech input/output through the incorporated LLM. CALM has achieved meaningful results when measured using evaluation metrics such as accuracy and response time, as well as manually validated characteristics including empathy, bias, engagement, and relevance. CALM effectively simplifies tasks, visualises learning and aligns solutions to the child’s interests.

articleTitle: DBSCAN and KMeans Clustering: Comparing Strengths and Suitability in Customer Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Data Science, Agents & Artificial Intelligence (ICDSAAI)
abstract: K-Means clustering and Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise, both unsupervised clustering approaches have many applications. This paper performs a comparative analysis of the suitability and strengths of these two methods in segmenting customers by emphasizing profession, annual income, spending score, family size, and work experience. With these parameters, K-Means clustering and Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise yielded the Silhouette Coefficients of 0.532 and 0.444 respectively. Such segmentation helps the marketing and sales team of a firm to plan and deliver personalized offers, promotions, rewards, and schemes to attract more customers and thereby increase revenues. The experimental analysis suggested that both methods are very effective in customer segmentation. The Silhouette Coefficient indicates the superiority of K-Means, but, Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise is more explanatory. The work also highlighted the benefits, differences, and suitability of both techniques.

Author Keywords: Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise
